texts: Sudden left-to-right shunting is not a cause of cyanosis in an adult with an isolated atrial septal defect: E.
Left-to-right flow sends oxygenated blood back to the lungs, so it overloads the right heart but does not lower arterial saturation.

Cyanosis needs right-to-left flow: Eisenmenger physiology, an inferior sinus venosus defect that lets IVC blood stream into the left atrium, or a large Eustachian valve directing IVC flow across the defect.
A pulmonary embolism can do it too, by raising right-sided pressure and reversing the shunt.
In the picture, the red water spilling into the blue lobby leaves the lips pink, while the four others turn them blue.
Memory hook: red into blue keeps the lips pink.
